items.informal_name: Continuity Preserves Strict Inequality in a Neighborhood
items.informal_description: For any point $x_0$ where functions $f$ and $g$ are continuous and $f(x_0) < g(x_0)$, there exists a neighborhood of $x_0$ such that $f(x) < g(x)$ for all $x$ in that neighborhood.

items.informal_name: Continuous Functions Differ at a Point iff They Differ in a Neighborhood in Hausdorff Spaces
items.type:
∀ {X : Type u_1} {Y : Type u_2} [inst : TopologicalSpace X] [inst_1 : TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y] {x : X}
  {f g : X → Y}, ContinuousAt f x → ContinuousAt g x → (f x ≠ g x ↔ ∀ᶠ (x : X) in nhds x, f x ≠ g x)
items.informal_description: Let $ Y $ be a Hausdorff space, and let $ f, g : X \to Y $ be functions continuous at a point $ x \in X $. Then $ f(x) \neq g(x) $ if and only if there exists a neighborhood $ U $ of $ x $ such that $ f(y) \neq g(y) $ for all $ y \in U $.

items.informal_name: Eventually f(x) < g(x) if Limits Satisfy y < z
items.informal_description: If functions $f$ and $g$ converge to limits $y$ and $z$ respectively with respect to filter $l$, and $y < z$, then there exists a neighborhood in $l$ such that for all $x$ in this neighborhood, $f(x) < g(x)$.

items.informal_name: Intermediate Value Theorem for Preconnected Spaces with Eventual Inequality
items.type:
∀ {X : Type u} {α : Type v} [inst : TopologicalSpace X] [inst_1 : LinearOrder α] [inst_2 : TopologicalSpace α]
  [OrderClosedTopology α] [PreconnectedSpace X] {a : X} {l : Filter X} [l.NeBot] {f g : X → α},
  Continuous f → Continuous g → f a ≤ g a → g ≤ᶠ[l] f → ∃ x, f x = g x
items.informal_description: Let $X$ be a preconnected topological space, and let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered topological space with an order-closed topology. Suppose $f, g : X \to \alpha$ are continuous functions. If there exists a point $a \in X$ such that $f(a) \leq g(a)$, and a non-bot filter $l$ on $X$ such that $g(x) \leq f(x)$ eventually in $l$, then there exists a point $x \in X$ where $f(x) = g(x)$.

items.informal_name: Intermediate Value Theorem for Continuous Functions on Order-Closed Preconnected Spaces
items.type:
∀ {X : Type u} {α : Type v} [inst : TopologicalSpace X] [inst_1 : LinearOrder α] [inst_2 : TopologicalSpace α]
  [OrderClosedTopology α] [PreconnectedSpace X] {l₁ l₂ : Filter X} [l₁.NeBot] [l₂.NeBot] {f g : X → α},
  Continuous f → Continuous g → f ≤ᶠ[l₁] g → g ≤ᶠ[l₂] f → ∃ x, f x = g x
items.informal_description: For a preconnected topological space $ X $ equipped with an order-closed topology, and for continuous functions $ f, g : X \to \alpha $ (where $ \alpha $ is a linearly ordered set), if there exist non-bot filters $ l_1 $ and $ l_2 $ on $ X $ such that $ f(x) \leq g(x) $ eventually in $ l_1 $ and $ g(x) \leq f(x) $ eventually in $ l_2 $, then there exists a point $ x \in X $ where $ f(x) = g(x) $.

items.informal_name: Characterization of Upper Semicontinuity at a Point
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [inst : TopologicalSpace α] [inst_1 : Preorder β] {f : α → β} {x : α},
  UpperSemicontinuousAt f x ↔ ∀ (y : β), f x < y → ∀ᶠ (x' : α) in nhds x, f x' < y
items.informal_description: A function $ f $ is upper semicontinuous at a point $ x $ if and only if for every $ y $ with $ f(x) < y $, there exists a neighborhood of $ x $ such that $ f(x') < y $ for all $ x' $ in that neighborhood.
